domain_label: Sweater Vertical — Yarn, Fibre & Line Architecture (Ludhiana sourcing → warm-California D2C)
purpose: A method for choosing the fibre, count, gauge and blend ratio of a small AI-designed D2C knitwear brand's 3-article line — sourced in/through the Ludhiana cluster and sold into warm-climate California/Turlock — and for specifying that yarn as an enforceable contract: which fibres and counts for the climate-first A1/A2/A3 line and why, where to buy (Ludhiana base vs imported premium tops), the realistic MOQ/price/lead-time bands, how to gate quality against pilling and returns, and the dyed-vs-outsource-dye call — without ever stating a fabricated named-firm price/MOQ/throughput as fact and tagging every money/capacity/performance/regulation claim FACT, ESTIMATE or UNKNOWN.
assumptions: no live per-mill quote is supplied; every price/MOQ/lead-time band is a labeled estimate (method = triangulated public reportage plus the inherited yarn-cost anchor) with a stated confidence, never a current-year point quoted as fact, and the underlying point-anchors (2018 merino, 2022 acrylic, 2024 cotton) are flagged stale

the market is warm-ish California / Turlock (hot summers, a narrow true-cold Nov-Feb window), which inverts Ludhiana's winter-woollen default and makes lightweight fine-gauge the core rather than the exception

Ludhiana sells product know-how, not its product mix; the in-cluster integrated spinners (Vardhman, Sportking, Nahar, Oswal) are a cited player roster, not a confirmed supplier contract for this brand
the operator is a micro-brand: posture is contractual QC written into the PO, not in-house metrology (a USTER tester is six-figure-USD class, exact list price unknown), and it never owns a dyehouse

fibre/count/gauge/weight metrics are dimensional identities or industry-lore order-of-magnitude bands from the SCOPE_GLOSSARY, applied as planning priors, not vendor-quoted constructions for this brand's exact swatches
exclusions: ocean India->US freight, landed cost, duty-paid math and US import-of-record mechanics beyond the fibre-driven duty-line fact (those belong to the logistics/unit-economics specialist)
knitting-machine selection, gauge capacity abundance, CAD/flat-knit programming and linking-throughput economics beyond the count->gauge match (those belong to the machines specialist)
post-knit finishing chemistry (mercerise, gas-singe, cellulase bio-polish, heat-set, milling) beyond naming it as the last pilling lever (that belongs to the finishing specialist)
stating a fabricated current-year point price, a named-dyer dye-lot MOQ, or a named-firm revenue/throughput as fact
brand positioning, CAC, pricing ladder and the default-fibre marketing call beyond the duty/cost/perceived-value mechanics of the blend ratio (those belong to the brand specialist)

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every price/MOQ/lead-time band in this KB: a triangulated public-reportage band with a stated confidence, never a current-year point quoted as fact; the underlying 2018/2022/2024 anchors are stale and a band must not feed a margin model without a live importer/mandi quote.

The fact that warm California/Turlock sells light/mid/transitional knits ~Sept-April and true heavy wool only Nov-Feb, flipping the line away from Ludhiana's winter-woollen default so the core is lightweight fine-gauge and wool is a thin seasonal capsule, not the base.

A1 cotton-blend 12GG 12-month core; A2 fine-acrylic 7-12GG value driver; A3 thin merino/lambswool Nov-Feb premium capsule (optional cashmere-blend halo) — the climate-first line, each article chosen as a fibre x count x gauge x weight quadruple.

The fibre proportion on the care label, the single biggest controllable decision: it moves cost, hand, warmth, care, perceived value and US import duty simultaneously, and must be written into the PO with a +/-3% by-mass tolerance verified by fibre-composition test to block cost-down drift and duty-misdeclaration.

The minimum dyed-yarn order per shade (~150-500 kg floor; dye-house economic ~500-2,000 kg; +20-50% small-batch surcharge below): at ~300-400 g/sweater, ~200 kg ~= 500-650 sweaters of one colour, so a micro-capsule affords only ~2-4 launch colours — the number that sizes the brand, not yarn price.

The mostly-independent quality controls set per article: staple length (longer=less pill), twist (TPM/TPI + S/Z or K; under-twist pills, over-twist spirals), ply (2-ply binds; singles skew a flat panel), fibre fineness (micron/dpf; the counter-intuitive finer=softer-but-pills-more dial), and blend ratio.

Where a yarn sits vs global production per parameter; 25% USTER (better than 75% of world output) on CVm% + IPI is the mainstream bar for mass acrylic/cotton, whereas demanding 5% USTER on a mainstream lot is unquotable or luxury-priced.

ICI Pilling Box (ISO 12945-1) grade 1-5; every anti-pill claim is gated at grade >=3-4 after at least one home-wash cycle because washing drops the grade and the post-wash grade is what predicts returns.

The rule that 2/30 (two 30s singles plied, resultant ~15s) versus 1/30 is a doubling error in fabric weight, and that a true 12GG hand comes from finer singles + fewer ends fed + a tighter knit confirmed at sampling, not from the folded-count label like '2/48 Nm'.

The non-negotiable posture that the micro-brand never owns dyeing: all Ludhiana CETPs were found non-compliant, CPCB levied crore-scale penalties and the NGT is reviewing the cluster, making dyeing the highest-regulatory-risk node with real closure exposure; launch on bought-dyed stock shades and graduate to job-work dye only for a proven hero colour.

The ladder is the lens every article and sourcing decision is read against.

cons.claim: A tier ladder is a design framing, not a measured demand curve, so it can ossify a fibre choice the market would revise

nodes.definition: Characterize each candidate fibre on the two dominant axes — staple length (longer -> less pill, stronger, smoother) and fineness (micron for animal, denier-per-filament for synthetic; finer -> softer) — so a fibre is chosen on properties, not its marketing word. Acrylic: cheap, bulky, bright-dyeing, machine-wash, moth-proof, but pills, static, weak wet-abraded [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, HIGH]. Wool: warm, elastic, but micron (not the word 'wool') decides prickle. Merino: ~17-24 um, sub-19.5 'fine/superfine' is the soft-but-wearable sweet spot. Lambswool: first-shearing grade, softer than later clips, sits below merino. Cashmere: ~14-19 um, extremely soft but pills more, luxury, blend-% only. Cotton: breathable, no-prickle, washable, but heavy and bags out (the warm-market go-to). Viscose/modal: drape and animal-fibre-cost cut. Nylon: a few % sharply improves pill+abrasion in a soft wool/cashmere blend [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, HIGH].

included: the staple-length and fineness axes
the hand/warmth/price/pilling/care profile per fibre
the article-vs-blend-ingredient marking for viscose/modal and nylon
excluded: the resultant count and gauge of each article

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a fibre grade availability or a property-driven complaint changes the selection logic

pros.claim: Selecting on micron/dpf and staple instead of the fibre's name prevents a soft-sounding word from hiding a pilling or comfort flaw
pros.example: specifying a micron ceiling rather than 'merino' so next-to-skin comfort is actually bought

cons.claim: The finer=softer axis is counter-intuitive on pilling and strength, so optimizing for hand alone can buy a worse-pilling yarn
cons.example: chasing the finest fibre for softness and getting a yarn that pills and breaks more

failure_modes: choosing a fibre by its marketing word and not its micron/staple/dpf
optimizing hand at the cost of pilling and strength without noticing the trade
acceptance_tests: each fibre is placed on the staple and fineness axes with its hand/warmth/price/pilling/care trade and its article-or-ingredient status, with the industry-lore tags carried
revisit_triggers: a finer or anti-pill grade of a fibre becomes available locally
a comfort or pilling complaint traces to a fibre choice
a blend-ingredient role (nylon %, viscose) is reconsidered

nodes.definition: Map yarn count (Ne/Nm/denier; pivot through Tex) and gauge (GG) to a target garment weight so the fibre x count x gauge x weight quadruple agrees (cross-team rule #4). 7GG ~ resultant Nm 6-8 (2/30, 2/24) -> the commercial-default mid pullover (~350-550 g) [FACT - GLOSSARY S3]; 12GG = the core fine tier (2/48 Nm-class for merino; high-Ne cotton) -> the warm-CA 'elevated basics' weight (~200-350 g) [FACT - GLOSSARY S3]. Weights are order-of-magnitude industry-lore bands. Higher GG -> finer, denser, lighter fabric needing finer yarn, and GG must match count; quote both plus the target GSM / grams-per-garment.

included: the 7GG and 12GG count-to-weight anchors
the GG-must-match-count and quote-GSM rule
the order-of-magnitude status of the weight bands
excluded: the folded-count doubling caveat (its own node)
the machine/programmer capacity to knit the gauge

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a sampling weight result or a gauge-weight band update changes the map

pros.claim: Forcing the quadruple to agree stops a vague 'midweight' brief that the factory cannot price or knit consistently
pros.example: specifying 12GG + high-Ne cotton + ~250 g together so the sampling target is unambiguous

cons.claim: The weight bands are order-of-magnitude industry-lore, not vendor quotes, so a precise gram target still needs sampling confirmation
cons.example: treating '12GG = 250 g' as exact when stitch length and construction move it

failure_modes: briefing a 'midweight' without fixing fibre, count, gauge and grams together
treating an order-of-magnitude weight band as a precise sampling guarantee
acceptance_tests: the 7GG and 12GG anchors are stated with their resultant-count classes and weight bands, the GG-matches-count rule is given, and the weight bands are flagged order-of-magnitude
revisit_triggers: a sampling result moves the achieved weight off the band

nodes.definition: Carry the classic spec caveat from the reconciler: do not quote '2/48 Nm = 12GG' as a rule. On resultant count, 2/48 Nm (~24 Nm) is barely finer than a 2/30 Ne cotton (~25 Nm); the move to a true 12GG hand comes from finer singles + fewer ends fed + a tighter knit confirmed at sampling, not from the folded-count label [ESTIMATE: MED]. Folded notation '2/30' = two 30s singles plied, resultant ~ singles / plies (~15s-equivalent), and the ends fed further multiply effective thickness. Misreading 2/30 vs 1/30 is a doubling error in fabric weight; confirm singles count + ply + ends fed before judging weight. Always pivot through Tex (Tex = 1000/Nm = 590.5/Ne) for any cross-count comparison.

included: the do-not-quote-2/48-Nm=12GG caveat
the resultant ~ singles/plies and ends-fed multiplier
the 2/30-vs-1/30 doubling-error warning and Tex pivot
excluded: the achieved garment weight bands themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a folded-count or conversion error or a sampling contradiction surfaces

pros.claim: Confirming singles + ply + ends fed before judging weight stops the most common doubling error in a naive PO
pros.example: catching a 1/30 quoted where a 2/30 was meant before it halves the planned fabric weight

cons.claim: The folded-to-resultant relationship is a guideline confirmed at sampling, not an exact predictor of hand
cons.example: assuming two yarns with the same resultant count knit to the same 12GG hand without sampling

failure_modes: quoting a folded label as a gauge rule and skipping the singles/ply/ends-fed check
comparing Ne and Nm without pivoting through Tex
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the 2/48-Nm caveat, the resultant-count and ends-fed relationship, the 2/30-vs-1/30 doubling-error warning and the Tex pivot
revisit_triggers: a sampling result contradicts a folded-count expectation

nodes.definition: Establish the blend ratio on the care label as the brand's #1 controllable lever: it moves cost, hand, warmth, care, perceived value AND US import duty simultaneously (wool 6110.11 ~16% vs cotton 6110.20 ~7%) [FACT - duty lines]. It is also a cheat-and-duty-risk surface, so it must be written into the PO with a tolerance — e.g. '70/30 +/-3% by mass, verified by fibre-composition test.' Blend drift is both a quiet supplier cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration exposure for the brand as importer of record [ESTIMATE: industry-lore, HIGH]. Even 5-10% cashmere lifts perceived value; a few % nylon is the cheapest pilling/abrasion lever in a soft wool/cashmere blend.

nodes.definition: Model A2, the value driver: fine acrylic / acrylic-rich blend at 7-12GG (2/30, 2/32 Nm-class; finer to 12GG), ~250-450 g. Its one fatal flaw is pilling — acrylic is the worst offender — so this article lives or dies on the anti-pill spec: an anti-pill / higher-dpf grade (~2.5 dpf), not the cheapest 1D, plus the contractual pilling gate. A2 is the cost floor and volume value position; without the pilling defence it becomes the return driver.

nodes.definition: Model A3, the seasonal premium capsule: merino or lambswool in a thin Nov-Feb drop (optional cashmere-blend halo), 7-12GG (merino 2/48 Nm-class), ~250-400 g. The climate demotes A3 from a base to a thin capsule — it justifies price without committing the line to heavy wool the warm market cannot sell. A few % nylon is the cheapest pill/abrasion lever in the soft-wool/cashmere blend.

nodes.definition: Name the five mostly-independent spinning dials, each mapping to one thing the customer feels, set per article's tier. (1) Staple length — longer -> less pill, stronger, smoother; name a minimum staple (mm) or fibre grade in the PO, not just the count. (2) Twist (TPM/TPI + S/Z, or twist-multiplier K) — the strength-vs-softness optimum; under-twist pills and breaks, over-twist feels wiry and causes spirality (the twisted-side-seam defect); knitwear-soft ~ K~3, require 'balanced ply'; the dial most often left blank in a naive PO. (3) Ply — 2-ply binds better than singles (singles skew/torque a flat panel, a QC reject); confirm singles count + ply + ends fed. (4) Fibre fineness (micron / dpf) — the counter-intuitive dial: finer = softer but pills MORE and is weaker; spec a micron ceiling (e.g. '<=19.5 um') not the word 'merino', and for acrylic an anti-pill / higher-dpf grade (~2.5 dpf), not the cheapest 1D. (5) Blend ratio +/- tolerance — the margin/positioning/duty lever; a few % nylon in a soft wool/cashmere blend is the cheapest pill+abrasion improvement.

conflict_axes.description: The warm climate caps the merino/lambswool capsule to a thin Nov-Feb drop while the premium fibre's margin and brand pull argue to size it bigger.
poles: size the premium capsule for margin
keep it a thin climate-bounded capsule
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the warm-climate calendar cap the capsule size and use the premium fibre to lift price, not to expand wool volume the market cannot sell

conflict_axes.name: fineness_for_hand_vs_pilling_strength
conflict_axes.description: Finer fibre is softer but pills more and is weaker, so optimizing hand fights the pilling and strength the defence must hold.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: spec a micron/dpf ceiling for hand but raise staple, twist, ply and an anti-pill grade to keep the ICI grade rather than chasing fineness alone

conflict_axes.name: yarn_price_small_vs_dye_lot_moq_binds
conflict_axes.description: Yarn fibre cost is small and well-anchored, tempting cost-as-lever, while the dye-lot MOQ per shade is what actually constrains the line.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat yarn price as small and non-binding and let the ~150-500 kg dye-lot MOQ (=> 2-4 colours) govern the line plan

conflict_axes.name: estimate_band_vs_fake_precise_point
conflict_axes.description: Stale point-anchors invite a fake-precise current price while the honest artifact is a labeled estimate band that must not feed a margin model raw.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: refuse stale points as current, keep the band with its confidence, and require a live importer/mandi quote before any margin use

conflict_axes.name: colour_breadth_vs_dye_lot_floor
conflict_axes.description: A brand wanting a broad palette pulls against the dye-lot floor that caps a micro-capsule at ~2-4 colours without surcharge.
poles: stay within the dye-lot colour floor
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: plan ~2-4 launch colours, share dye lots across styles, and reserve a proven hero colour before paying a small-batch surcharge

conflict_axes.name: tight_uster_clause_vs_quotable_mainstream_lot
conflict_axes.description: Demanding too tight a USTER percentile prices a mainstream lot out, while too loose a clause lets defects through.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: demand 25% USTER on CVm%+IPI for mainstream acrylic/cotton (never 5%), reserving tighter percentiles for genuinely premium lots

conflict_axes.name: bought_dyed_simplicity_vs_job_work_colour_control
conflict_axes.description: Bought-dyed stock shades are simplest and push risk to the supplier but limit colour control versus greige+job-work dyeing.
poles: greige plus job-work dye for control
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: launch on bought-dyed stock shades and graduate to greige+job-work dye only for a proven hero colour worth the dye-lot MOQ and shade-management

conflict_axes.name: micro_spinner_moq_flex_vs_self_test_capability
conflict_axes.description: Micro-spinners flex MOQ further but cannot self-test, while integrated spinners can hit USTER clauses at higher MOQ.
poles: use a micro-spinner for MOQ flex
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use micro-spinners for non-gated greige flex but push any quality-gated lot to a USTER-equipped spinner or budget a third-party lab

conflict_axes.name: duty_favourable_ratio_vs_desired_positioning
conflict_axes.description: A cotton-rich duty-favourable blend ratio pulls against a wool-forward positioning the brand may want.
poles: set the ratio for low duty
set the ratio for the desired fibre story
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: default the core ratio to the duty-favourable cotton-rich class and shift toward wool only in the premium capsule where the story justifies the higher duty

edge_cases.description: A stale point-anchor (2018 merino, 2022 acrylic, 2024 cotton) is fed into a margin model as a current price
edge_cases.trigger: someone reads a band's underlying point as today's quote
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse the point as current, keep the labeled band, and require a live importer/mandi quote before any margin use

edge_cases.description: A0 PO quotes '2/48 Nm = 12GG' as a rule and mis-sizes the fabric weight
edge_cases.trigger: a folded-count label is treated as a gauge equivalence without confirming singles+ply+ends-fed
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm singles count + ply + ends fed and reach 12GG via finer singles, fewer ends fed and a tighter knit at sampling, not the folded label

edge_cases.description: A 1/30 is supplied where a 2/30 was meant, halving the planned fabric weight
edge_cases.trigger: a doubling error in folded notation passes into the PO
edge_cases.mitigation: state singles/ply/ends-fed explicitly in the count clause and reject lots whose resultant count is off

edge_cases.description: A cheap 1D acrylic value article pills and drives returns
edge_cases.trigger: the cheapest acrylic grade is specced without the anti-pill/higher-dpf grade or pilling gate
edge_cases.mitigation: spec an anti-pill / ~2.5 dpf grade and gate at ICI >=3-4 post-wash before shipping the value article

edge_cases.description: A 5% USTER clause is demanded on a mainstream acrylic/cotton lot and the order becomes unquotable or luxury-priced
edge_cases.trigger: an over-tight percentile is written into a mass-fibre PO
edge_cases.mitigation: demand 25% USTER on CVm%+IPI for mainstream fibres and reserve tighter percentiles for premium lots only

edge_cases.description: An 'anti-pill' claim is accepted without a post-wash ICI test and pills after the customer washes it
edge_cases.trigger: the pilling claim is gated dry or not at all
edge_cases.mitigation: gate every anti-pill claim at ICI box grade >=3-4 after at least one home-wash cycle

edge_cases.description: More launch colours are planned than the dye-lot floor supports, incurring small-batch surcharges or dead stock
edge_cases.trigger: a broad palette is planned past the ~2-4 colour ceiling
edge_cases.mitigation: plan ~2-4 colours, share dye lots across styles, and reserve a proven hero colour before adding more

edge_cases.description: The brand owns a dyehouse and takes on closure-grade NGT/CPCB regulatory risk
edge_cases.trigger: a captive dyeing node is considered for colour control
edge_cases.mitigation: never own a dyehouse; launch on bought-dyed stock shades and use job-work dye only for a proven hero colour

edge_cases.description: A bought-dyed stock-shade re-order arrives off-shade and there is no shade-match clause to reject it
edge_cases.trigger: a lot-to-lot shade drift on a re-order
edge_cases.mitigation: write a shade standard, lot-to-lot delta-E and fastness minima into the PO and reject off-shade lots against them

edge_cases.description: A launch drop is committed into the Jul-Oct cluster peak and the lead time stretches
edge_cases.trigger: a bulk knit/link/finish run is scheduled in the contention window
edge_cases.mitigation: do not commit a launch drop into the peak; schedule bulk outside Jul-Oct and reserve linking capacity

edge_cases.description: A quality-gated lot is placed with a micro-spinner that cannot produce a USTER report
edge_cases.trigger: MOQ flex is prioritized over self-test capability for a gated article
edge_cases.mitigation: push the gated order to a USTER-equipped integrated spinner or budget a third-party lab spot-check per lot

edge_cases.description: Blend drift moves a 70/30 toward a different ratio, cutting cost and mis-declaring the duty class
edge_cases.trigger: no blend tolerance is written into the PO so the supplier drifts the ratio
edge_cases.mitigation: write '+/-3% by mass, fibre-composition verified' into the PO and test composition before accepting the lot

workflow.action: Establish the warm-climate inversion and selling calendar
workflow.description: State the ~Sept-April light/mid season and the Nov-Feb heavy-wool window and the lightweight-core consequence
workflow.gate: the selling calendar and the inversion away from winter-woollen are stated with the direction tagged estimate

workflow.description: Order acrylic->cotton->merino/lambswool->cashmere and mark articles vs blend ingredients
workflow.gate: the tiers are ordered and each fibre is marked article or blend-ingredient

workflow.action: Characterize each fibre on the hand/warmth/price/pilling/care axes
workflow.description: Place each fibre on the staple-length and fineness axes with its trade-offs
workflow.gate: each fibre has its staple/fineness profile and article-or-ingredient status with honesty tags

workflow.action: Map count and gauge to garment weight
workflow.description: State the 7GG and 12GG count-to-weight anchors and the GG-matches-count rule
workflow.gate: the 7GG and 12GG anchors and weight bands are stated as order-of-magnitude with the GG-matches-count rule

workflow.description: Carry the do-not-quote-2/48-Nm caveat and the 2/30-vs-1/30 doubling-error warning
workflow.gate: the resultant-count and ends-fed relationship and the doubling-error warning are stated

workflow.action: Set the blend ratio as the #1 lever with a tolerance
workflow.description: Show the ratio moves cost/hand/warmth/care/value and duty and mandate the +/-3% by-mass clause
workflow.gate: the duty lines are cited and a +/-3%-by-mass fibre-composition-verified tolerance is mandated

workflow.description: State each article's fibre x count x gauge x weight quadruple, role and gate
workflow.gate: each article names its quadruple, role and the duty or pilling gate that decides it

workflow.description: Put everyday fibres in-cluster and import only the premium ceiling, with the integrated-spinner roster
workflow.gate: the in-cluster default and import-only-premium lists are stated with FACT/ESTIMATE tags and the micro-spinner limit

workflow.action: Estimate the price, MOQ and lead-time bands
workflow.description: Give per-fibre price bands, the dye-lot MOQ and the lead-time bands as labeled estimates
workflow.gate: every band carries a confidence and the stale-anchor flag, and the dye-lot MOQ is identified as binding

workflow.action: Convert the dye-lot MOQ into the colour-starved line plan
workflow.description: Plan ~2-4 colours, share dye lots and reserve a hero colour
workflow.gate: the plan prescribes ~2-4 colours with shared dye lots robust within the 150-500 kg floor

workflow.action: Specify the five spinning dials and the pilling defence
workflow.description: Set each dial per article and order the pilling defence by control
workflow.gate: the five dials and the most-controllable-first pilling order are stated with the vendor % downgraded

workflow.action: Gate quality and write the PO sheet, then make the dye call and the merged verdict
workflow.description: Demand 25% USTER and ICI >=3-4 post-wash, enumerate the PO sheet, choose bought-dyed-no-dyehouse, and compose the go/no-go
workflow.artifact: PO sheet + dye call + line verdict
workflow.gate: the PO sheet enumerates every gate, the dye call launches on bought-dyed stock shades, and the verdict conditions each article go on its binding gate

priority_rationale: The climate inversion, fibre tier ladder and per-fibre selection logic come first because every article and sourcing choice depends on the warm-market calendar and the fibre property axes; the count-gauge-weight map, folded-count discipline and blend-ratio lever next, because they are the metrics that turn a fibre choice into a buildable quadruple and the single biggest controllable lever; the three articles then apply that to A1/A2/A3; the sourcing split, price/MOQ/lead-time bands and the colour-starved line plan next, because they expose the dye-lot MOQ as the binding commercial constraint; the spinning dials, pilling defence and the USTER/ICI gate then make quality an enforceable contract; and the PO sheet, dye-sourcing call and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into an attachable PO and a defensible build/avoid verdict.

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any price/MOQ/lead-time claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no live quote is supplied and the point-anchors are stale, so a band may never be presented as a current fact
dominance_rules.trigger: any rupee/kg, kg-MOQ or week figure is stated
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-with-confidence, flag the stale anchor, and require a live importer/mandi quote before any margin use

dominance_rules.rule: The dye-lot MOQ dominates yarn price as the binding constraint
dominance_rules.rationale: yarn fibre is only ~$1-2.50/garment and well-anchored, while the dyed-shade MOQ sizes the brand's colour count
dominance_rules.trigger: a line decision is driven by yarn price
dominance_rules.action: re-anchor the decision on the ~150-500 kg dye-lot MOQ (=> 2-4 colours), not yarn price

dominance_rules.rule: The post-wash ICI pilling gate dominates any anti-pill adjective
dominance_rules.rationale: washing drops the grade and the post-wash grade is what predicts returns
dominance_rules.trigger: an 'anti-pill' claim is made without a wash test
dominance_rules.action: gate the claim at ICI box grade >=3-4 after at least one home-wash cycle or reject it

dominance_rules.rule: The 25% USTER bar dominates a tighter percentile for mainstream lots
dominance_rules.rationale: 5% USTER on a mass acrylic/cotton lot is unquotable or luxury-priced
dominance_rules.trigger: a percentile tighter than 25% is written into a mainstream-fibre PO
dominance_rules.action: default to 25% USTER on CVm%+IPI and reserve tighter percentiles for genuinely premium lots

dominance_rules.rule: The no-captive-dyehouse rule dominates any colour-control argument
dominance_rules.rationale: dyeing is the highest-regulatory-risk node with crore-scale CPCB penalties and NGT closure exposure
dominance_rules.trigger: owning a dyehouse is proposed for colour control
dominance_rules.action: launch on bought-dyed stock shades and use job-work dye only for a proven hero colour

dominance_rules.rule: The blend tolerance dominates the unspecified care-label ratio
dominance_rules.rationale: blend drift is both a supplier cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration exposure for the importer of record
dominance_rules.trigger: a blend ratio is stated without a tolerance
dominance_rules.action: write +/-3% by mass, fibre-composition verified, and test before acceptance

dominance_rules.rule: Singles+ply+ends-fed confirmation dominates the folded-count label
dominance_rules.rationale: 2/30 vs 1/30 is a doubling error and the folded label does not fix the hand
dominance_rules.trigger: a folded count is read as a gauge or weight equivalence
dominance_rules.action: confirm singles count + ply + ends fed and reach the target gauge at sampling, not by the label

dominance_rules.rule: Self-test capability dominates micro-spinner MOQ flex for gated lots
dominance_rules.rationale: a micro-spinner that cannot produce a USTER report cannot satisfy a quality-gated clause
dominance_rules.trigger: a quality-gated order is placed for MOQ flex with a micro-spinner
dominance_rules.action: route the gated lot to a USTER-equipped integrated spinner or budget a third-party lab

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate label and confidence to every price/MOQ/lead-time band when it is first produced
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stale band circulating as a current fact and being retracted out of a margin model

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm singles + ply + ends fed before judging fabric weight from a folded count
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a 2/30-vs-1/30 doubling error mis-sizing the fabric after the PO is placed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Spec the anti-pill/higher-dpf grade and the post-wash ICI gate before shipping the acrylic value article
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a cheap-acrylic pilling-return problem surfacing after launch

anti_rework_rules.rule: Plan to ~2-4 colours against the dye-lot floor before committing the line plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a broad-palette plan eating small-batch surcharges or carrying dead stock

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the +/-3% blend tolerance and fibre-composition test into the PO from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: blend drift becoming a quiet cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration corrected after import

anti_rework_rules.rule: Use 25% USTER (not 5%) on mainstream lots when the clause is first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unquotable or luxury-priced mainstream order that has to be re-tendered

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide bought-dyed stock shades and no captive dyehouse before any colour-control build
anti_rework_rules.prevents: taking on closure-grade NGT/CPCB risk that must later be unwound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Schedule bulk outside the Jul-Oct cluster peak when setting the drop calendar
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a launch drop stalling on stretched peak lead time and contended linking capacity
